result.summary: 本文提出了“精度感知”的缩放定律，将训练和推理中的低精度效应纳入损失预测 [abstract]。作者提出低精度训练会降低模型的有效参数量，从而可以预测低精度训练和后训练量化带来的额外损失 [abstract]。对于推理，后训练量化带来的退化随训练数据量增加而增大，最终使额外的预训练数据变得有害 [abstract]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在最高 1.7B 参数、26B token 的模型上验证了预测 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：精度、参数量和数据之间存在怎样的权衡，以及这些权衡在预训练和推理中有何不同 [S1.p1]。原文指出，精度是影响成本和性能的第三个重要因素，但当前的缩放定律并未考虑这一点 [S1.p1][abstract]。

evidence.quote: Specifically, we ask: What are the tradeoffs between precision, parameters, and data? How do they compare for pretraining and inference?
However, the precision in which models are trained and served is an important third factor that contributes to both cost and performance.
Low precision training and inference affect both the quality and cost of language models, but current scaling laws do not account for this.

method.text: 论文提出“精度感知”的缩放定律，其核心思想是假设比特精度和参数量可以互换地贡献于模型的“有效参数量” N_eff，而量化实现细节仅通过影响该量来与损失缩放交互 [S1.p2]。作者将训练和推理的缩放定律统一为单一函数形式，以预测不同精度下训练和推理带来的退化 [abstract][S5.p8]。

evidence.quote: This functional form that posits bit precision and parameter count interchangeably contribute to a model’s “effective parameter count,” $N_{\text{eff}}$, and implementation details like which parts of a model are quantized to what precision, interact with loss scaling only through their effect on this quantity.
We unify the scaling laws for post and pretraining quantization to arrive at a single functional form that predicts degradation from training and inference in varied precisions.

Modeling low-precision effects during pretraining as independent and multiplicative noise that accumulates, and including post-training quantization degradation, the predicted loss for a language model with $N$ parameters, trained on $D$ tokens, with training precision $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}$ to end-time weight-precision $P_{\text{post}}$, can be predicted as $L(N,D,P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}},P_{\text{post}})=AN_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha}+BD^{-\beta}+E+\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$

experiments.text: 作者在 Dolma V1.7 数据集上训练和评估了一系列 OLMo 风格的模型，使用标准 Transformer++ 实现 [S2.SS3.p1]。实验扫描了 N ∈ [30,60,110,220] 百万参数和 D ∈ [1.5,3,6,13,26] 十亿 token，对每个 (N,D) 组合启动超过 20 次运行，并扫描了 8 个精度值 [S2.SS3.p1]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在最高 1.7B 参数、26B token 的模型上验证预测 [abstract]。

evidence.quote: We train and evaluate a suite of OLMo-style models on the Dolma V1.7 dataset, using a standard Transformer++ implementation
Our experiments consist of a sweep of language model pretraining runs over $N\in[30,60,110,220]$ million parameters (non-embedding) and $D\in[1.5,3,6,13,26]$ billion tokens.
we train up to a very high $D/N\approx 10^{3}$ to study data scaling and set off over 20 runs at every $(N,D)$: we sweep 8 values of precision for each of the (weights, activations, attention).
We fit on over 465 pretraining runs and validate our predictions on model sizes up to 1.7B parameters trained on up to 26B tokens.

findings.text: 后训练量化带来的损失退化随数据量增加而增大，对于固定模型，在某个点之后继续用更多数据训练，如果模型之后会被量化，可能反而有害 [S3.p1][S3.F2]。在量化感知训练中，权重的比特精度可以与参数量进行权衡，即较小 N 但较大 P_w 的模型可以达到与较大 N 但较小 P_w 的模型相同的损失，且精度增益在较低精度时较大，在约 6-7 比特后饱和 [S4.SS1.p1]。对于低精度训练，权重、激活和注意力的量化效应是组合且乘性的 [S4.SS2.p1]。计算最优的预训练精度通常与计算预算无关，但如果模型大小 N 被约束，计算最优精度随计算量缓慢增长，P* ∝ log C [S4.SS3.SSS2.p2][S4.SS3.SSS3.p1]。统一缩放定律表明，在较低精度下训练的模型对后训练量化更鲁棒，即退化更低 [S5.p1]。

evidence.quote: We quantify the resulting loss degradation $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$, finding that post-train quantization scales poorly in data.
We can see that degradation grows with data, bottom row is fitted with Equation 2. For $D/N$ sufficiently large (left), loss can increase in data.

We observe that the bit precision of the weights can be traded off for the number of parameters, i.e., a model with smaller $N$ but larger $P_{\text{w}}$ can achieve the same loss as a model with larger $N$ but smaller $P_{\text{w}}$.
Additionally, we find that the gains from increasing the bit precision of the weights are large at lower precisions but saturate at higher precisions (typically around 6-7 bits per weight).
The Effects of Quantizing Weights, Activations, and Attention are Compositional and Multiplicative
We find that scaling fits on integer type are a strong fit until 4-bit precision, at which points the difference between the two types becomes more apparent.
Surprisingly, our scaling laws predict that models of differing sizes should not necessarily be trained in the same precision, and that compute-optimal precision scales as $P^{*}(C)\propto\log C$.

We find two competing effects at play when predicting $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$, but overall, models trained in lower precision are more robust to post-train quantization in the sense of incurring lower degradation.

limitations.text: 作者指出，分析中使用了固定架构来考察精度、参数和 token 的影响，而低精度训练通常涉及架构调整，可以缩小与普通全精度模型的差距 [S6.p2]。其次，虽然计算成本随精度线性缩放，但由于系统开销，减半精度带来的收益通常不到 2 倍 [S6.p2]。第三，只考虑了损失缩放，没有下游模型评估 [S6.p2]。作者强调所发现的趋势旨在提供启示而非规定性结论，并希望未来工作能在更大模型规模上更全面地检验这些效应 [S6.p2]。

evidence.quote: First, we use a fixed architecture throughout to examine the effects of precision, parameters, and tokens in a controlled manner. In contrast, low precision training often involves architectural tweaks that can close much of the gap from a vanilla full precision model.
Second, while compute costs do scale linearly with precision, the gains from halving precision are usually less than 2x due to systems overhead.
Third, we only consider loss scaling without downstream model evaluations.
We emphasize that the trends we find aim to be suggestive rather than prescriptive, and hope future work can more comprehensively examine these effects at larger model scale.

issues.quote: The Effects of Quantizing Weights, Activations, and Attention are Compositional
